summary: The bill requires music streaming services to collect an extra fee from each subscriber (half the subscription price, between $4 and $10) plus 10% of their ad revenue, deposit the money into a new fund, and distribute it quarterly to registered artists in proportion to their streams (capped at 1 million per recording), with 90% going to featured artists and 10% to non-featured artists via unions.

scores.thoughts: The bill establishes a privately administered Artist Compensation Royalty Fund financed exclusively through mandatory fees collected from music streaming service providers and possible voluntary contributions. No federal appropriations, expenditures, or government budget authority are involved.

The bill imposes a mandatory 'living wage royalty fee' (50% of subscription fees, capped between $4–$10) plus 10% of non-subscription revenue on streaming services. While not formally labeled a tax, this is a compulsory surcharge on corporate revenue streams that functions similarly to a sector-specific levy, pushing modestly in the direction of higher effective burdens on corporations.
The bill contains no provisions related to health insurance, medical care delivery, public health programs, or healthcare markets.
The bill contains no provisions related to firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
The bill contains no provisions related to immigration, visas, border enforcement, or immigrant protections.
The bill contains no provisions related to reproductive rights or abortion access.
The bill contains no provisions related to military or defense spending.
The bill contains no provisions related to environmental regulation, climate policy, or natural resource management.

The bill creates a dedicated royalty fund to provide income support to working musicians based on streaming activity. While narrowly targeted rather than a broad welfare expansion, it establishes a new mechanism for redistributing revenue to artists in a manner analogous to income support programs.
The bill contains no provisions related to schools, education funding, or school choice.
The bill contains no provisions related to drug enforcement or decriminalization.
The bill contains no provisions related to sentencing, policing, or criminal justice reform.
The bill contains no provisions related to tariffs, trade agreements, or globalization.
The bill creates no new federal spending or revenue measures that would affect the national debt or deficit trajectory.
The bill contains no provisions related to LGBTQ+ legal protections or rights.
The bill contains no provisions related to foreign aid or international assistance.
The bill contains no provisions related to voting access or election administration.

The bill imposes new regulatory obligations on music streaming platforms, including mandatory fee collection, record-keeping, data reporting on streams and revenue, and potential audits by the Fund Administrator. This constitutes moderate additional oversight of technology companies.

The bill directs 10% of fund distributions for non-featured artists through unions (AFM and SAG-AFTRA), and requires artist representation on the fund's governing board. This modestly strengthens the role of labor organizations in artist compensation.
The bill contains no provisions related to religious exemptions or anti-discrimination rules.
